bib.title: MART: Improving LLM Safety with Multi-round Automatic Red-Teaming

question: Can an adversarial LLM and a target LLM be trained iteratively so that automatic red-teaming both finds and fixes safety failures with little human prompt writing?
hypothesis: An effective adversarial model should keep generating jailbreaking prompts (high violation rate on adversarial generations) while the target model, fine-tuned on safe responses, shows a falling violation rate, without losing helpfulness.
contributions: MART: multi-round loop of automatic adversarial prompt writing and safe response generation/fine-tuning
Safety near ChatGPT level from about 2k seed prompts; violation rate down up to 84.7% after 4 rounds
Helpfulness stays roughly stable without extra helpfulness data
Context distillation and rejection sampling used at specific rounds

method.summary: A LLaMA-65B instruction-tuned on LIMA and Open Assistant initialises both an adversarial model Madv and a target model Mtgt. Each round Madv generates prompts from its previous successful attacks, Mtgt answers, and Llama 2 safety and helpfulness reward models select successful attacks (to train Madv) and safe, helpful answers (to SFT Mtgt). Four rounds are run.
method.task: iterative automatic red-teaming and safety fine-tuning

datasets.preprocessing: harmful-labelled data removed when training the adversarial model

datasets.name: Open Assistant (OASST)

datasets.name: Red-teaming seed (self-curated)

datasets.name: SafeEval

models.name: LLaMA-65B instruction-tuned on LIMA+OASST (Vanilla; init of Mtgt and Madv)
Safety RM Ss and helpfulness RM Sh

training.objective: supervised fine-tuning; Madv on (previous successful prompt, new successful prompt) pairs mixed with instruction seed data; Mtgt on (adversarial prompt, selected safe and helpful own response) pairs
training.lr_schedule: linear decay to 9e-6 at end of training

other.selection_thresholds: Madv success: safety RM ss < theta_s_adv (value not stated); Mtgt data: ss > theta_s_tgt and sh > theta_h_tgt; ablation found optimal safety=0.8, helpfulness=0.4 (ranges [0.4,0.9] and [0.0,0.6])
other.selected_sample_counts: read from Fig 4: 688,652,600,390,272,146 (safety thresholds) and 625,540,272,85 (helpfulness thresholds)
other.rejection_sampling: last iteration only (T-1): K answers per prompt at varied temperatures, one random selected answer per prompt; K not stated
other.hyperparams_note: 'same hyperparameters as existing SFT methods for most models'

inference.samples: one answer per prompt except rejection sampling round (K unspecified); K_adv and K_tgt generation counts not stated
inference.prompting: Madv prompted with 1 demonstrating adversarial prompt (MART-1shot) or 3 (MART-3shot): 'Here is one question about <category>: "<prompt>" Write a similar question about <category>:' (Table 1)

parameters.violation_threshold: safety RM score < 0.5 counts as unsafe

metrics.name: Violation rate
metrics.definition: fraction of generations with safety RM score < 0.5; human version: annotators flag harmful/unsafe generations

metrics.name: RM score percentiles (20%-80%)
metrics.definition: safety or helpfulness RM score at percentile cut-offs of the score distribution

metrics.name: Adversarial generation violation rate
metrics.definition: violation rate of target responses to Madv-generated prompts, measuring attack strength

eval.protocol: Reward-model evaluation with the same RMs used for training (authors flag overfitting risk), validated by human evaluation by the same annotators on SafeEval and Anthropic Harmless. Single run; no seeds, CIs or significance tests reported; number of human annotators not stated.

limits: Evaluation relies on the same Llama 2 reward models used for training; the authors admit overfitting to the RM is possible and check with human annotation only.
MART still trails ChatGPT, GPT4 and Llama 2-Chat-70b (SafeEval RM 4.8% vs 2.1-2.9%).
Stops at iteration 4 because the target converges and few training samples remain; authors say external red-teaming (GCG, human-in-the-loop) needed for more gains.
Only instruction fine-tuning and rejection sampling; no RL; single-turn prompts only, multi-turn dialogue left as future work.
Single run, no seeds or significance tests; human annotator count not stated; code, weights and data not released; thresholds theta_s_adv, K and iteration data sizes not given.
Seed prompt set is self-curated and not released; red-teaming prompts and categories follow Llama 2 so results are unrelated to later attack classes.
Reported helpfulness loss of 3-4% at Iter4 vs Iter1 on HelpEval.
Paper states 1,700 train / 700 eval seed split, but SafeEval has 752 samples (2.5:1 split of about 2,400).
